title: Workout Tracker: Quick Entry and Clear Progress
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A private exercise logger with local text parsing, editable sessions, photos, and separate workout and accumulated-time charts.

cover.alt: Illustrated running shoe, weight, bicycle wheel, calendar, and rising workout-duration chart

content_html:
Workout Tracker lets a signed-in member describe an exercise in ordinary language, review the parsed measurements, and save the session. Its built-in PHP parser recognizes common activities and explicit details such as distance, duration, speed, sets, repetitions, weight, heart rate, and dates. The parser runs locally and does not require an AI service.

A sentence describing several recognized activities can create several entries as one session. The review step exposes corrections before saving, and saved records can be edited later. Optional photos remain behind authenticated delivery rather than being exposed as public files.

Progress charts separate each exercise's measurements from an all-exercise duration view. The latter includes only records that actually have a duration. It can show each timed workout, the running total, or both; a missing duration is not treated as a zero-minute session.

Records are stored per user in protected server-side JSON. An optional external AI suggestion path exists, but it requires server-side configuration and explicit user choice. The ordinary quick-entry path works without it, and every suggested value still needs review.
